clue.text: Greek character overdue with catalogue for collector

parts.note: phi is a letter of the Greek alphabet
something overdue is late
a catalogue is a list

explanation.surface: A collector is browsing a catalogue of Greek items, and is running late.
explanation.walkthrough: The collector meant is one of stamps.
explanation.definitionFit: A philatelist is a stamp collector.

clue.text: Height on bladed pole of frost

indicators.note: in a down clue, one piece placed on another sits above it

parts.note: an oar is a pole with a blade at the end

explanation.surface: A tall pole with a blade is covered in frost.
explanation.walkthrough: 'of' is a link word joining the wordplay to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Hoar is white frost, as in hoar-frost.

clue.text: Lear set about another Shakespearean

indicators.note: about signals that the letters are moved around into a new order

explanation.surface: King Lear wanders about on the set alongside another character from the plays.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' rearranges LEARSET. Laertes is Ophelia's brother in Hamlet, so like Lear he is a Shakespeare character.
explanation.definitionFit: Laertes is a character in Hamlet, written by Shakespeare.

clue.text: The sort to make an impression

definitions.meaning: a sort is a kind or category
to strike keys so letters are printed on paper

explanation.surface: Someone describes the kind of person who wants to impress.
explanation.definitionFit: A type is a kind, and to type is to press keys that print characters, making an impression.

clue.text: One 24 found protection on pond

parts.note: 24 is LADY; Lily is one lady's name
a pad is protective padding

explanation.surface: A woman found shelter beside the pond.
explanation.walkthrough: The cross-reference sends you to 24, LADY, and Lily is an example of a girl's name; 'found' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: A lily pad is the floating leaf of a water lily, seen on ponds.

clue.text: One's lamenting inclusion of bang

indicators.note: inclusion of says the letters are contained inside the words before

explanation.surface: Someone grieving takes in a loud bang.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters sit across ONE'S LAMENTING.
explanation.definitionFit: A slam is a loud bang, like a door shut hard.

clue.text: An alarming person

parts.note: read as someone who deliberately spreads alarm, not someone frightening to look at

explanation.definitionFit: A scaremonger spreads frightening rumours, alarming people on purpose.

clue.text: Make provision and support for the young creature

parts.note: to cater is to provide food or what is needed
a pillar is a supporting column

explanation.surface: Someone provides for and supports their child.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for' is a link word; the young creature is the larva of a butterfly or moth.
explanation.definitionFit: A caterpillar is the larval stage of a butterfly or moth.

clue.text: HMS Belfast, say, an armoured vessel

definitions.text: HMS Belfast, say, an armoured vessel

parts.words: HMS Belfast, say, an armoured vessel
parts.note: a description of a large heavily armed warship, with HMS Belfast, the cruiser moored in London, given as an example

explanation.definitionFit: A capital ship is one of a navy's largest and most heavily armed warships.

clue.text: In reprisal damaging a toy trailer

indicators.note: damaging suggests the letters are knocked out of shape into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone smashes a toy trailer to get revenge.
explanation.definitionFit: A retaliatory act is one done in revenge.

clue.text: Not long before arriving at fault

indicators.note: before places the first piece ahead of the second

parts.note: not long means short
arriving means coming

explanation.surface: Someone arrives late, as they always do, which is a fault.
explanation.definitionFit: A shortcoming is a flaw or failing.

clue.text: Cleaner seat I vacate

indicators.note: to vacate is to leave, so the I named moves out of the word for a seat

parts.note: a chair is a seat

explanation.surface: A cleaner asks someone to get out of the chair.
explanation.walkthrough: A char is British slang for a cleaning lady, short for charwoman.
explanation.definitionFit: A charwoman, or char, is a woman employed to clean houses.

clue.text: Get involved with mum after yours truly

indicators.note: after places mum's letters following those of yours truly

parts.note: yours truly is a jokey way of saying me
mum means silent, and sh is a call for silence

explanation.surface: Someone tells their mother to get involved after them.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mum' is not mother but quiet, as in 'keep mum'.
explanation.definitionFit: To mesh is to engage or interlock, as gears do.

clue.text: Rota included single revel

indicators.note: included puts the single letter inside the word for a rota

parts.note: a rota is a roster of duties
I, the Roman numeral one, means single

explanation.surface: A rota had a single night out on it.
explanation.definitionFit: To roister is to make merry noisily.

clue.text: Wheel knocking top off small spade

indicators.note: knocking top off removes the first letter, the top of a down entry

parts.note: a trowel is a small hand tool like a spade

explanation.surface: A wheel strikes a small spade and knocks its head off.
explanation.definitionFit: A rowel is the small spiked wheel on a spur.

clue.text: Monthly weather report in London

definitions.note: the definition names a place found in London

parts.note: May is one month
fair is a weather forecast word for good weather

explanation.surface: A monthly forecast of the weather for the capital.
explanation.walkthrough: Mayfair is a wealthy district of central London.
explanation.definitionFit: Mayfair is an upmarket district in central London.

clue.text: Encountered engineers at some length

parts.note: encountered means met
RE is the Royal Engineers, the British army corps

explanation.surface: Someone ran into engineers at length.
explanation.definitionFit: A metre is a unit of length.

clue.text: Thus got ahead having done some work at last

definitions.text: having done some work at last

parts.note: thus means so
to have got ahead is to have led

explanation.surface: Someone finally got ahead after doing some work.
explanation.walkthrough: A last is a cobbler's foot-shaped block: work at the last means putting soles on shoes, not finishing.
explanation.definitionFit: A shoe that has been soled has had a sole fitted on the cobbler's block.

clue.text: It might be ground for lunch

definitions.meaning: lunch is one of the day's ...

explanation.surface: Something ground up to eat at midday.
explanation.definitionFit: Meal is milled grain such as oatmeal, and lunch is an example of an eating occasion.

clue.text: Fellow is concerned initially with public revenue

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: initially picks the opening letter of concerned

explanation.surface: A fellow is worried about tax money.
explanation.definitionFit: The fisc is a state's treasury or exchequer.

clue.text: Earth's violent interior

indicators.note: violent suggests the letters are thrown into disorder

parts.note: the possessive s adds no letter

explanation.surface: The planet's core is violent.
explanation.definitionFit: The heart of something is its centre or core.

clue.text: Having reached the peak one can go no higher

definitions.text: Having reached the peak one can go no higher

parts.words: Having reached the peak one can go no higher
parts.note: sounds like a remark about a career at its peak, but read literally it is about standing on a summit

explanation.definitionFit: A hilltop is the summit, above which you cannot climb.

clue.text: Tyre oddly having enough tread

indicators.note: oddly picks the first and third letters of tyre

parts.note: ample means enough

explanation.surface: A tyre has plenty of tread left.
explanation.definitionFit: To trample is to tread heavily on something.

clue.text: One of a pair of breathers

definitions.text: One of a pair of breathers

parts.words: One of a pair of breathers
parts.note: breathers suggests rest breaks, but here it means openings for breathing

explanation.definitionFit: Each nose has two nostrils, the openings that air passes through.

clue.text: Maturer sort of mistake

indicators.note: sort of hints at a rough version, with the letters put in a new order

explanation.surface: An older person's kind of mistake.
explanation.definitionFit: An erratum is an error, especially in print.

clue.text: Torn veil that's no good

indicators.note: torn shows the word is ripped apart and put back in another order

explanation.surface: A ripped veil is useless.
explanation.definitionFit: Evil is wickedness, the opposite of good.

clue.text: Young man with youth leader, a female

parts.note: a lad is a young man

indicators.note: leader picks the first letter of youth

explanation.surface: A young man accompanied by a youth leader who is a woman.
explanation.definitionFit: A lady is a woman, especially a well-bred one.

clue.text: Lightning dash

explanation.surface: A very quick sprint.
explanation.definitionFit: A thunderbolt strikes in a storm, and to bolt is to dash away.

clue.text: Islands in Ireland or just one in Scotland, we hear

indicators.note: we hear says the word is to be spoken out loud

parts.note: Arran is a single island in the Firth of Clyde

explanation.surface: Several islands off Ireland, but only one off Scotland, apparently.
explanation.walkthrough: The Aran Islands lie off Galway in Ireland; Arran, spelt with two Rs, is a Scottish island pronounced the same.
explanation.definitionFit: The Aran Islands are a group off the west coast of Ireland.

clue.text: Six-footer I opposed

parts.note: an ant is an insect with six legs, so a six-footer

explanation.surface: A tall person says they are opposed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Six-footer' suggests a tall person; it is an insect with six feet.
explanation.definitionFit: Anti means against.

clue.text: Separate some of the cast

parts.note: some of a thing is part of it
a theatre's cast is its company of actors

explanation.surface: Some actors in a play go their own ways.
explanation.definitionFit: To part company is to go separate ways.

clue.text: I'm with petty cash becoming compassionate

indicators.note: becoming signals the letters change into something new

explanation.surface: Someone handing over petty cash is kind.
explanation.definitionFit: Sympathetic means showing compassion.
